# Reflection

## What I Kept, Revised, and Rejected

**Kept (and why):** Technical CSS scaffolding suggestions; saved time on plumbing.

**Revised (what changed and why):** Initial color palette suggestions; too saturated, tuned down to maintain friction tone.

**Rejected (and why):** All easing-curve suggestions; all "feel better" UX recommendations.

## Reflection

**What did I learn from this project that I would not have learned without AI?**
> That my aesthetic instincts are sharper when I have a default to push against.

**What did I learn despite using AI?**
> That rejection is editorial.

**What would I do differently next time?**
> Write the Position Statement with even more specificity about what "friction" means.

**Where was I most tempted to accept AI output uncritically, and why?**
> Around accessibility tradeoffs; felt unsure, AI sounded authoritative.

## AI Disclosure Statement

> This work was produced through structured human-AI collaboration using Claude 4. Alex Rivera directed all design decisions, including layout, motion, and accessibility tradeoffs. The AI contributed technical CSS scaffolding and initial color palette suggestions. 5 Records of Resistance document specific decisions to reject or revise AI suggestions.
